question: Why do builders in Veridia care so much whether ordinary people like the look of their buildings?
answer_fact: Public ratings set an aesthetics charge within each building's land tax, so pleasing designs pay less and are more profitable.

question: At the concert, why did some other guy in a purple robe suddenly bolt for the exit when Gladias was called out?
answer_fact: A member of the public deliberately drew the crowd's attention onto himself so Gladias could get away.

question: Why weren't Zei and Fin in the room that took the full force of the blast during their physics lesson?
answer_fact: A man moved the class at the last minute to a different room one floor up, which saved them.

question: Why does Mov make Gladias change into a different robe before they go meet the stranger?
answer_fact: In case something on his old robe lets him be tracked; Arctic spy devices are increasingly slipping into Veridia.

question: Why was Zei willing to take a trip abroad with his rival right before their final match?
answer_fact: Traveling together means neither can secretly study more, so both can rest; plus he and his mom get a cheap first trip abroad.

question: How did Gladias get rid of the footage the big man at the concert had taken of his face?
answer_fact: He distracted the man, grabbed his device, ordered it to wipe recent media and restart, and it deleted four files including his face.

question: What does Delwart actually ask Gladias to do?
answer_fact: Choose the Keeper track instead of Sentinel and vote to remove every rubric he encounters.

question: What was the hidden twist in Zei's quarter-final game?
answer_fact: Teams were not chosen randomly; he was deliberately paired with Bai as a test of whether they would cooperate.

question: What did Gladias see happen just as Delwart walked away from their table?
answer_fact: Someone else in a privacy robe left the neighboring booth and followed Delwart.

question: When people rate buildings on that minus-five to five slider, why doesn't it help to just give everything extreme scores?
answer_fact: Each voter's ratings get normalized to average zero and fixed spread, so only honest relative strength matters.

question: How does the system punish Order members who let slip what they're working on?
answer_fact: Anyone can submit a guess of a member's task with a deposit; if right, the member's pay is cut and the guesser gets half.

question: How do the cities in the United Cities get a say in each other's governments?
answer_fact: Paired cities elect part of each other's parliament: larger city gets the agreed share; smaller gets it divided by square root of size ratio.

question: Who are Febric and Hreda, and why are they living with Gladias and Seila?
answer_fact: They are Vil and Daia's kids; the two co-families take turns raising all four children for half a year each.

question: What's the history between Zei and Bai before the tournament game?
answer_fact: Bai had beaten Zei all three times over past years and gloated about it, even taunting him about the prize money.

question: Who is the man Seila is with when the Dzego kids meet her in Freetown?
answer_fact: Jahn, whom Seila introduces as her friend; he is a Freetown local.

question: What was Gladias's score as a trainee at the concert, and what did he need to keep it above?
answer_fact: His score was 92; staying above 90 would let him become a Sentinel or Keeper.

question: Which social media company was cutting off outside apps, making the citizens' panel angry?
answer_fact: Bluewhale, which now only lets verified hardware connect, supposedly to stop spam.

question: Why did Gladias give up on becoming a Sentinel and go for the Keeper role instead?
answer_fact: He says Keepers hold the real power to change things because rubrics matter more; Mov suspects Delwart persuaded him.

question: Why couldn't Gladias pay for his lunch the first time he tried?
answer_fact: He had forgotten to move money to himself; most of his funds were only reachable from home or via social recovery.

question: Why is the little library at the square west of Galanar full of books nobody wants to read?
answer_fact: Mov says owners exploit a tax rubric by adding facilities that technically qualify but nobody uses, likely to keep kids away.

question: Why do Dzego's language priests spend so much effort reworking their language instead of the economy or the army?
answer_fact: Progress in economy or military gets bombed by the Arctics, while language work is harmless and even impresses them.

question: Why did Den and Mu decide to tell Zei the real purpose behind the strategy game?
answer_fact: They needed to explain why he should study cryptography and still compete, lest he guess on his own and tell others.

question: How did Bai trick Zei early in the city final?
answer_fact: She had her AI ignore the diagonals as bait while building strong defenses there herself, so Zei's diagonal attack failed.

question: What did Zei get in his prize bag after the final that Bai didn't?
answer_fact: A dark purple letter marked as meant only for Zei to read.

question: How did the senators' vote on admitting Gladias to the Order turn out?
answer_fact: The senators split evenly ten to ten, and the Chairman cast the deciding vote in favor.

question: What did Eighteen find when he swept the booth before Gladias's second Keeper meeting?
answer_fact: A tiny needle-shaped spy device hidden beneath a bump in the table.

question: How big are the panels that Keepers work in, compared with Sentinel panels and court panels?
answer_fact: Keepers deliberate in three groups of seven, Sentinels in three groups of three, and courts use five judges.

question: How can an ordinary buyer be sure their chip comes from the same supply the inspectors test?
answer_fact: Both buy through a physical mixnet of sealed, coded boxes, so the maker cannot tell which chips go to inspectors.

question: How could Gladias borrow money at the restaurant without revealing who he was?
answer_fact: A zero-knowledge proof backed by his work reviews revealed only a one-time hash and the loan amount, never his name.

question: Who is the robed man Zei meets in a sealed room deep inside the mountain pyramid?
answer_fact: He is Den, a High Council member of the Kungaupei.

question: What happened to Bai's parents, and who brought her up?
answer_fact: Both died in a lab explosion when she was small; she lived with an aunt who largely neglected her.

question: What changed for Mov after the random selection picked him?
answer_fact: He was chosen to become a Herald next term, so he no longer holds any formal power.

question: How many years had Gladias been an Acolyte by the time of his hearing before the senators?
answer_fact: Four years, with a prediction score in the ninety-fourth percentile.

question: What was the symbol count when Bai gave up the city final?
answer_fact: Zei led twelve symbols to six when Bai resigned.

question: Why does Deluin invite Zei to Redshire?
answer_fact: He is flying home for his parents' birthdays and coaching; if Zei comes too, Deluin can justify skipping the coaching.

question: Why did Vil and his old coworkers take that hedge fund to court?
answer_fact: Divergent's owners secretly owned Jump and bet against it, so its collapse let them avoid paying staff bonuses and severance.

question: Why does Gladias suggest the Keepers hold off two months before deciding on the military tech change?
answer_fact: After Mov's report made him suspicious, he wanted no change; waiting lets an Arctic attack, or none, settle the question.

question: Why did the organizers scrap the Minpentai final instead of just pushing it back?
answer_fact: Su says more games would be wrong now, and they don't want to give false hope or distract people.

question: Why does Zei only offer Deluin help from 'smart people' he knows instead of naming the secret groups behind him?
answer_fact: Revealing them to an outsider in occupied land would break confidentiality, and he couldn't fully trust the connection yet.

question: How does Veridia tax buildings with stuffy indoor air?
answer_fact: It's part of land tax: nothing for perfect air, up to a third of a percent yearly if rooms average over 1000; filters raise limits.

question: How can a foreigner like Deluin pick up the Dzegojan language so fast?
answer_fact: Dzegoban has only 256 roots, so it can be learned in under a month well enough to get around.

question: How does Gladias's voting setup stop Delwart from checking which way he voted?
answer_fact: No one, even Gladias, knows which keys are valid; only totals are decrypted, so he can't prove his votes.

question: How did Zven score the winning point in his Helisport match?
answer_fact: He handed the instructor the forgotten fourth ball, which had broken rotors and lay on the ground.

question: What happened when the Arctics took over Redshire?
answer_fact: Drones, aircraft and a land force from hidden tunnels overran Redshire within two longhours; the leaders' planes were shot down.

question: What did Mov overhear when he secretly listened in on Delwart's next meeting?
answer_fact: Delwart and a hardware-openness Keeper plotted to sway that Keeper's group, giving Delwart contacts in two groups on one rubric.

question: How did Zei work out his opening setup when the game was suddenly played on hexagons?
answer_fact: Inspired by his textbook, he ran the rules in reverse from the desired end state, undoing each step like a hash permutation.

question: Where is Deluin from, and how did he end up in Dzego's championship?
answer_fact: He is from Redshire and is one of four foreign players brought in this year.

question: What does Deluin now believe about complimenting a country on its scenery?
answer_fact: He once saw it as a backhanded insult but now thinks beautiful nature takes great human effort to maintain.

question: How many qualifying games did Deluin win?
answer_fact: Deluin won all six of his six qualifying games.

question: What score did Hreda get on her math test?
answer_fact: She scored ninety-six percent.
